claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A hybrid framework can combine a sparse set of DFT-derived descriptors with calibrated analytical surrogate models.
Elastic constants, misfit volumes, unstable stacking-fault energies, and surface energies are suitable key descriptors for deformation and fracture in hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework can rapidly and accurately predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness in hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
A minimal set of high-fidelity first-principles calculations can support surrogate prediction over a broader alloy space and reduce the need for exhaustive calculations.
Chemical fluctuations and phase boundaries in the hierarchical heterostructure mediate local bonding and slip mechanisms.
Embedded physical descriptors capture essential elastic- and plastic-deformation physics.
Combining physical descriptors with an analytical model can improve interpretability and transferability relative to black-box machine learning.
The hybrid method is expected to reduce runtime by more than 50% relative to full DFT/CALPHAD workflows.
The hybrid method is expected to improve prediction accuracy by approximately 10–20% over traditional high-throughput DFT and CALPHAD methods.
High-throughput first-principles workflows for multi-principal-element alloys have high computational demands.
Purely data-driven or black-box alloy models can require large, well-covered datasets, lack interpretability, and remain primarily interpolative.
Existing computational approaches struggle specifically with predicting fracture toughness.
The model is intended to remain applicable from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures provided the hierarchical heterostructure remains stable.
Reliability will diminish when local chemical heterogeneity or phase behavior falls outside the descriptor range represented during training.
Significantly higher temperatures or non-standard loading conditions can activate mechanisms absent from calibration and reduce reliability.
The precise quantitative gains in accuracy and efficiency are uncertain until tested on blinded experimental data.
A blinded prospective benchmark would compare predictions for held-out hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 samples with tensile and fracture measurements.
Failure to improve prediction error by at least 10–20% or to reduce computation time by at least 50% would falsify the hypothesis.
